about_blocks.text: About The Healing Institute at Taylor Bay
about_blocks.html: About The Healing Institute at Taylor Bay

about_blocks.text: The Healing Institute is a private residential treatment centre for addiction, mental health concerns and concurrent disorders. Since March 2026 it has run from 240 Davis Road on Gabriola Island, British Columbia, on the island's northwest shore at Taylor Bay. The centre began on Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay, and its own blog announced the completed move to Gabriola that month, with admissions open and programming carried on without a break.
about_blocks.html: The Healing Institute is a private residential treatment centre for addiction, mental health concerns and concurrent disorders. Since March 2026 it has run from 240 Davis Road on Gabriola Island, British Columbia, on the island's northwest shore at Taylor Bay. The centre began on Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay, and its own blog announced the completed move to Gabriola that month, with admissions open and programming carried on without a break.

about_blocks.text: The property covers 6.77 acres with 426 feet of shoreline, coastal forest and walking trails. It has several buildings for lodging and programs and a fitness centre. The site is shared with The Haven, the not-for-profit learning centre that has been on the same land since 1983 and still runs its own programs there. The Healing Institute bought the campus from the Haven Foundation.

about_blocks.text: Treatment is planned around each person after an assessment. Counsellors run individual and group sessions, psychoeducation, relapse prevention, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and Dialectical Behaviour Therapy. Medical and nursing staff handle health checks, medications and medically supported withdrawal management when someone needs it, under Medical Director Jackie Muth, a nurse practitioner with opioid agonist treatment certification.

about_blocks.text: The rest of the day mixes in yoga, movement, mindfulness, art therapy and time outside on the shoreline and trails. The centre also lists an infrared sauna, a cold plunge and IV therapy, and meals are cooked on site by Executive Chef Andrew Hewson, who taught at SAIT for 18 years.

about_blocks.text: Every participant gets lifetime access to continuing care once residential treatment ends, and a continuing care coordinator helps plan the return home. Families can join the free Family Freedom Program on Zoom every Monday at 5:30 p.m. Pacific. The centre is part of ROSC Solutions Group, which runs addiction and recovery services across Western Canada. It is private and fee based, it does not publish prices, and admissions offers a free 15-minute consultation by phone or online booking.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About The Healing Institute

faqs.question: Where is The Healing Institute now?

answer_blocks.text: The Healing Institute is at 240 Davis Road on Gabriola Island, BC, at Taylor Bay on the island's northwest shore. It moved there from Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay and announced the move as complete on March 12, 2026. The campus is shared with The Haven, which still runs its own programs on the site.

It moved there from Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay and announced the move as complete on March 12, 2026. The campus is shared with The Haven, which still runs its own programs on the site.

faqs.question: How do I get to Gabriola Island?

answer_blocks.text: Gabriola is reached by a BC Ferries crossing of about 20 minutes from downtown Nanaimo to Descanso Bay. From Vancouver, take the Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay ferry to Nanaimo first, so the whole trip usually takes 3 to 4 hours with sailing waits. Ask admissions about arrival times before you book.

faqs.question: What level of care does The Healing Institute offer?

answer_blocks.text: It is a residential program, so you live on site for the length of treatment. Medical and nursing staff provide medically supported withdrawal management when it is needed, and lifetime continuing care follows discharge. The centre does not list a standalone outpatient program.

answer_blocks.text: The centre's website does not publish a fixed length. Its recovery.com profile gives a typical stay of 6 to 8 weeks, with residential stays ranging from 14 to 90 days. Admissions will confirm the length once your assessment is done.

faqs.question: Does The Healing Institute offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, in a supported form. The program page says medical and nursing care includes medically supported withdrawal management when required, along with assessment, medication management and health monitoring. Tell admissions what you are using so they can plan this before you arrive.

faqs.question: How much does The Healing Institute cost?

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not publish its fees on its website or on recovery.com. It is a private, fee-based program, and admissions goes over costs during a free 15-minute consultation. A Medicard partner logo on the site suggests financing may be available, so ask about it when you call.

faqs.question: Is The Healing Institute publicly funded?

answer_blocks.text: No, it is a private centre and does not describe any coverage through Island Health or another BC health authority. Some extended health or employer plans may reimburse part of private treatment, so check your plan and ask admissions for the paperwork you would need.

faqs.question: What conditions does The Healing Institute treat?

answer_blocks.text: It treats addiction, mental health concerns and concurrent disorders. Its recovery.com profile lists alcohol, opioids, cocaine, methamphetamine, benzodiazepines and prescription drugs among the substances, and anxiety, depression, PTSD and trauma among the mental health conditions.
